title: Customer support that never starts from scratch
description: Give every ticket its full context, answer with evidence, escalate cleanly, and turn repeated questions into better support.

navigation.title: Customer Support & Success
navigation.tagline: Every ticket, promise, and next step in context

introduction: The slow part of customer support is rarely the reply. It is reconstructing the case: finding the full conversation, checking the account, searching the product docs, seeing whether the bug is known, and working out what the customer was promised.

Strawberry gives one companion that whole trail across your help desk, inbox, CRM, docs, team chat, billing, and issue tracker. A ticket can arrive ready to answer, escalate, or turn into engineering work—with the sources and next owner attached.

sections.title: What can you hand off today?

blocks.text: Bring Strawberry the customer work already in front of you. Your companion will pick the smallest useful Support or Success workflow and show you the result before anything is sent or changed.

skill.context: Start with a real customer case, account, or goal and choose the most useful next result.

blocks.text: A ticket says what the customer wrote today. The answer may live in last month's meeting, a CRM promise, a usage change, or a Slack thread about a known issue. Strawberry pulls the pieces together and keeps every claim close to its source.

items.title: See goals, usage, and open promises
items.text: Build a grounded account view without hiding gaps behind a health score.

skill.context: Review the customer's progress, current signals, evidence gaps, and next actions.

items.title: Walk into the next call caught up
items.text: Turn the account history and open decisions into a short brief for a check-in, QBR, renewal, or escalation.

skill.context: Prepare for a customer conversation using the account context that could change it.

items.title: Leave the call with owners and next steps
items.text: Carry reliable notes into customer follow-up and the internal actions that now need an owner.

skill.context: Preserve the decisions, commitments, and follow-through from a customer conversation.

sections.title: Draft the right answer, with the evidence attached

blocks.text: Drop in a ticket or point Strawberry at the queue. Your companion can check the complete thread, the customer's history, current product docs, known issues, and the team's real policy before it recommends a reply.

items.title: Triage the queue by impact
items.text: Make the priority, owner, next action, and first response clear without inventing a universal severity score.

skill.context: Triage this customer request using the team's actual rules and current context.

items.title: Draft answers from current sources
items.text: Reconcile product docs, help content, account history, and prior cases into a customer-ready response.

skill.context: Find the strongest available answer and prepare a response for this customer and channel.

blocks.text: Once you approve the route and boundaries, Strawberry can recognize when a case needs another team and prepare the handoff automatically. The human gets the impact, timeline, evidence, work already tried, current customer message, and exact decision they need to make—not a link to a mystery ticket.

items.title: Send a human the full case
items.text: Package the customer impact and the specific investigation, exception, or decision the receiving team needs to own.

skill.context: Prepare the customer-impact brief, current communication, exact internal ask, and next owner.

items.title: Create Jira or Linear issues from support tickets
items.text: Reproduce the problem, check for duplicates, and prepare a grounded engineering issue without leaking private customer context.

skill.context: Research and report the product bug while keeping customer-specific context appropriately scoped.

items.title: Keep ownership visible until it is fixed
items.text: Track the next update, unresolved decision, and verified resolution across Support and the specialist team.

skill.context: Track the owners and unresolved commitments behind a customer escalation.

blocks.text: Customer Success should begin with the outcome the customer bought, not a generic product tour. Strawberry can turn the signed scope, sales notes, stakeholders, setup dependencies, and success measures into one owned path to value.

items.context: Turn agreed goals and commitments into an owned path to first value.

blocks.text: A good answer should not disappear when the ticket closes. Publish a verified resolution for the next customer, or show Product the pattern across several cases with the original examples still linked.

items.title: Publish the answer once
items.text: Turn a verified resolution or recurring question into clear, findable help content without creating a duplicate article.

skill.context: Turn verified current behavior into clear, findable customer documentation.

items.title: Show Product the recurring pattern
items.text: Group feedback into themes, tensions, examples, and gaps without pretending the summary decides the roadmap.

skill.context: Turn customer feedback into themes, tensions, examples, and gaps with clear links to the sources.

blocks.text: Start with one real case. Correct the sources, tone, routing, ownership, and review points until the result feels like your team. Then keep the method instead of rebuilding it in the next chat.

items.title: Set up the connected support system
items.text: Map the stack, learn from resolved cases, test the focused skills, and propose Routines only after the manual flow works.

skill.context: Use Strawberry's published support method as a starting point, then adapt it to the systems and decisions your team already trusts.

items.title: Share the method with the team
items.text: Preserve a trusted workflow as a team skill when colleagues should follow the same sources, boundaries, and handoffs.

skill.context: Turn a trusted customer workflow into a shared team method with clear context, ownership, review points, and stop conditions.

blocks.text: Add a Routine only after the job works manually. A schedule can repeat the queue check or weekly learning review; it does not create permission to send, refund, change an account, file an issue, or publish.
